description: Fix cosmetic 'Loop' header ghosting on tmux pane reflow by clearing the frame on width-change in the dashboard poll re-render path.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: useStdout() returns { stdout, write }; stdout exposes .columns for pane width and write() writes raw data straight to stdout. No Ink 7 breaking change affects raw-escape writes; the existing resize path already writes CURSOR.clear escapes directly and this fix stays on that raw-escape approach rather than instance.clear()/rerender. Fetch returned a partial page.

userStories.title: Clear frame on width-change in dashboard poll re-render path
userStories.description: As a cam operator watching the dashboard in a tmux pane, I need the poll-driven re-render to fully clear the frame when the pane column width changes so that the 'Loop' summary header stops ghosting/stacking ~20 orphaned copies after a pane reflow (SIGWINCH burst).
acceptanceCriteria: The dashboard tracks the column width (stdout.columns) used at the last paint; on the poll-driven re-render (src/ui/Dashboard.tsx:144-149), when the current width differs from the last-paint width, a full-frame clear is written before the repaint using the existing CURSOR.clear escape (\x1b[H\x1b[J from src/commands/dashboard.ts:64), not a hand-rolled escape. [oracle: grep -q 'CURSOR.clear' src/ui/Dashboard.tsx]
In steady state (width unchanged between poll ticks) no clear is written on the poll path (zero flicker); the assertion is exercised by the unit test below. [oracle: bun test]

The existing makeResizeClearer resize-event clear path (src/commands/dashboard.ts:970-1005) and its 'resize' listener registration are left intact as belt-and-suspenders. [oracle: grep -q 'makeResizeClearer' src/commands/dashboard.ts]

A deterministic unit test in test/dashboard.test.ts drives a column-width change between poll ticks via an injectable seam (injected writeFn/stdout, no real tmux) and asserts CURSOR.clear is written exactly when the width changed and NOT when the width is unchanged, following the existing fake-writeFn pattern (test/dashboard.test.ts:899-990). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Verify the screen renders correctly (dashboard still mounts and repaints normally under ink-testing-library; no regression to the steady-state frame). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: PRIMARY FILE: src/ui/Dashboard.tsx. Width is already read at line 133 via `const { stdout } = useStdout();` -> `const cols = stdout?.columns ?? 80;`. The poll path is the setInterval->setData useEffect at lines 144-149; that repaint currently writes NO clear (the root cause). Add last-paint width tracking (a ref) and, when the poll re-render observes a different width, write CURSOR.clear BEFORE the repaint. KEY THE DETECTION ON WIDTH (stdout.columns), not height (gotcha: there is no app-side line-count to compare; Ink's stale previous-frame line-count is internal). SEAM: source width from useStdout()/an injected stdout and add an injectable writeFn prop to DashboardAppProps (useStdout() also returns a `write` method) so the unit test can deterministically drive a width change and assert the escape write; writing a raw escape from inside the React component is a layering smell, so keep it behind the injectable seam. REUSE CURSOR.clear from src/commands/dashboard.ts:64 (import it; do not hand-roll \x1b[H\x1b[J). Do NOT switch to instance.clear()/rerender/patchConsole (the Ink instance is used only for waitUntilExit(); staying with raw CURSOR.clear matches the existing resize path and avoids a broader refactor). Leave makeResizeClearer (dashboard.ts:970-1005) and the process.stdout.on('resize', ...) registration (dashboard.ts:1038-1039) untouched. TESTS: test/dashboard.test.ts:899-990 already fakes writeFn + a fake clock and asserts what makeResizeClearer WRITES; mirror that shape for the new poll-path test. GOTCHA (patterns.md): Ink tests here must call installTerminalSizeMock() (test/helpers/mock-terminal-size.ts) so renders don't shell out to `tput` and flake (CAM-201); and lastFrame() line-matching against the 'Loop' summary block can false-match story-id substrings printed in that panel -- disambiguate by a marker unique to the target line (CAM-66 US-001 bullet in scripts/cam/patterns.md). If you introduce any injectable timer handle, type it as `unknown` and fence the cast in default wrapper fns (CAM-66 makeResizeClearer precedent; ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> is unsafe in this repo) -- but a width-change clear likely needs no timer at all. COSMETIC-ONLY: no loop-correctness impact; the real-tmux visual is an informal, non-blocking post-ship eyeball (operator elected deterministic-test-only verification). Ink success/failure is the glyph, not divider color -- irrelevant here but do not regress it.
